where_to_go: Work Orders → open a work order
what_to_do: Check line prices, totals, Finance card, Stats tab.
expected_result: All money visible. Service Manager has See Financial Data ON.
spec_reference_plain: Per the spec: a role with 'See Financial Data' ON (which the Service Manager role has) must see every dollar figure on a work order — line prices, the Rate/Margin/Total columns, the Financial Info card, the Stats tab money, and the Finance tab invoice. [Ref: SV-5319 Custom Roles permission matrix; checklist Service Manager row #9 'Pricing shows (See Financial ON)']
expected_plain: Logged in as a Service Manager, every price and dollar amount on a work order should be visible, nothing hidden or blanked.
actual_result_plain: Opened work order S9-24661 as Tech-with-Service-Manager. All money was visible everywhere. The left Financial Info card showed Parts $0.00, Labor $929.72, Shop Supplies $97.62, Subtotal $1,027.34, GST $51.37, Total $1,078.71, Balance $1,078.71. The Lines grid showed the Rate ($232.43), Margin (100%) and Total ($929.72) columns with values. The Stats tab showed the Hours, Labor, Parts and Total breakdowns with Sell price/Cost/Margin/% dollar figures ($929.72 sell, $0 cost, 100% margin). The Finance tab showed the full invoice INV-S9-24661 with Labor $929.72, Parts $0.00, Shop supplies $97.62, Subtotal $1,027.34, GST(5%) $51.37, Total $1,078.71 and Balance $1,078.71. Nothing was hidden or masked.
notes: See Financial Data confirmed ON in the Service Manager fe-permissions (seeFinancialData:true). Money confirmed on Lines, Financial Info card, Stats tab and Finance tab.

where_to_go: Work Orders → open a work order → Finance tab
what_to_do: Create an invoice / process a payment.
expected_result: Allowed. Service Manager has Invoicing and Payments Create and Edit.
spec_reference_plain: Per the spec: a role with Invoicing and Payments = Create and Edit (which the Service Manager role has, permission invoicingPaymentsCreateAndEdit) may create invoices and process/record payments on a work order's Finance tab. [Ref: SV-5319 permission matrix; checklist Service Manager row #10 'SM can create invoices/payments']
expected_plain: As a Service Manager you should be able to create an invoice on a not-yet-invoiced work order and record a payment on an invoiced one.
actual_result_plain: On the Finance tab of not-yet-invoiced work order S9-24669 a 'Create Invoice' button was present and enabled. On the Finance tab of already-invoiced work order S9-24661 a 'New Payment' button was present; clicking it opened the payment dialog exposing 'Make Payment' and 'Send to Terminal' controls (i.e. the payment action was reachable, not blocked). Both the invoice-creation and payment-processing actions were available to the Service Manager.
notes: Confirmed invoicingPaymentsCreateAndEdit is ON for the Service Manager. Evidence: 'Create Invoice' on S9-24669 Finance tab and 'New Payment' -> Make Payment dialog on S9-24661 Finance tab. Controls left un-submitted to avoid unnecessary data churn; the front-end gate (button present + dialog reachable) is the permission proof.

where_to_go: Work Orders → Finance tab → an invoice/payment
what_to_do: Try to reverse an invoice / delete a payment / void a transaction.
expected_result: BLOCKED. Service Manager has Invoicing and Payments = View/Create and Edit, NO Delete.
spec_reference_plain: Per the checklist: a Service Manager has Invoicing and Payments = View plus Create-and-Edit but NOT Delete (no invoicingPaymentsDelete), so it should be blocked from reversing/voiding an invoice or deleting a payment. NOTE: this row is stale under spec v33 — reversing a work-order invoice was re-gated to Work Orders: Delete (see case N2 and SV-8093). [Ref: SV-5319 permission matrix; checklist Service Manager row #11 'SM cannot delete/reverse (no Invoicing Delete)']
expected_plain: As a Service Manager you should NOT be able to reverse an invoice, delete a payment, or void a transaction — those controls should be hidden or should error.
actual_result_plain: The Service Manager was NOT blocked from reversing. On the Finance tab of both an invoiced work order (S9-24661) and a paid one (S9-24656), the invoice actions menu (the three-dots menu next to New Payment) showed 'Reverse' and 'Issue Credit', both enabled. Clicking 'Reverse' opened a confirmation modal titled 'Warning' reading 'This action will re-open and undo the invoice. Are you sure you want to proceed?' with active Reverse and Cancel buttons — i.e. the reversal is fully available (I clicked Cancel/closed without confirming). No separate 'delete payment' or 'void transaction' control was surfaced anywhere, but because the reverse action is available the case's expected outcome (blocked from reversing) does not hold.
replication_steps_plain: 1. Log in as the Tech user who has the Service Manager role. 2. Go to Work Orders and open an invoiced work order (e.g. S9-24661). 3. Click the Finance tab. 4. Click the three-dots (more) menu at the top-right of the invoice, just left of 'New Payment'. 5. Observe the menu shows 'Reverse' and 'Issue Credit'. 6. Click 'Reverse'. 7. Observe a 'Warning' pop-up appears saying the invoice will be re-opened/undone with a working 'Reverse' button — the action is allowed, not blocked. Expected per checklist: this should have been blocked/hidden.
notes: STALE row per spec v33 (superseded by N2). The staging Service Manager role actually includes workOrdersDelete (confirmed in fe-permissions), and under v33 invoice reversal is gated by Work Orders: Delete, so 'Reverse' is available to SM. The checklist premise 'no Invoicing Delete blocks this' no longer determines the outcome. Related: SV-8093.

feature_area: Reverse invoice - now needs WO/Part Sales Delete (v33)
what_to_do: Try to reverse a WO invoice.
expected_result: BLOCKED. Reversing a WO invoice now requires Work Orders: Delete (v33). SM has WO = View/Create and Edit, NO Delete. (Previously framed as Invoicing Delete.)
spec_reference_plain: Per spec v33 (SV-8093): reversing a work-order invoice is gated by the Work Orders: Delete permission. The checklist asserts the Service Manager has Work Orders = View/Create-and-Edit but NOT Delete, so it expects reversal to be BLOCKED. [Ref: SV-8093; checklist Service Manager row N2 'SM cannot reverse WO invoice (no WO Delete)']
expected_plain: As a Service Manager you should NOT be able to reverse a work-order invoice, because the checklist says the role lacks the Work Orders: Delete permission that reversing now requires.
actual_result_plain: The Service Manager WAS able to reverse a WO invoice. On the Finance tab of work order S9-24661, the invoice three-dots menu showed 'Reverse'; clicking it opened a confirmation modal ('Warning: This action will re-open and undo the invoice. Are you sure you want to proceed?') with an active Reverse button. The reversal action was fully available (I clicked Cancel, did not complete it). This contradicts the expected BLOCKED result. Root cause: the staging Service Manager role actually HAS the Work Orders: Delete permission (workOrdersDelete is present in the role's fe-permissions), so the v33 WO-Delete gate lets it reverse. The checklist's assumption that SM lacks WO Delete is not true for this staging role.
replication_steps_plain: 1. Log in as the Tech user assigned the Service Manager role. 2. Open Work Orders and pick an invoiced work order (e.g. S9-24661). 3. Open the Finance tab. 4. Click the three-dots menu next to 'New Payment' at the top-right of the invoice. 5. Click 'Reverse'. 6. Observe the 'Warning' confirmation pop-up with a working Reverse button — the reversal proceeds, it is NOT blocked. Expected per checklist: reversal should be blocked because SM lacks Work Orders: Delete.
notes: NEW (v33) - refines struck row #24 logic for SM. Ref SV-8093 (https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-8093). Key finding: the system-default Service Manager role on staging (role_id a5bfcb60-2af7-47b1-938b-d0d1d101340b) DOES include workOrdersDelete, contradicting the checklist's stated SM permission set. So the v33 gating works correctly (reverse follows WO Delete), but the role configuration grants SM that permission, making the expected BLOCKED result wrong for this role.

where_to_go: Work Orders → open a work order → header
what_to_do: Change mileage, lead tech, customer, asset.
expected_result: Allowed. Service Manager has Work Orders Create and Edit.
spec_reference_plain: Per the spec: a role with Work Orders = Create and Edit (which the Service Manager role has, workOrdersCreateAndEdit) may edit a work order's header fields (lead technician, service advisor, customer, asset). NOTE: this row is flagged STALE in v33 — mileage/engine hours etc. are now gated by Work Order Lines: Create and Edit (see case N1). SM holds both. [Ref: SV-5319 permission matrix; checklist Service Manager row #12 'SM can edit WO header fields']
expected_plain: As a Service Manager you should be able to change work-order header details like mileage, the lead technician, the customer, and the asset.
actual_result_plain: On work order S9-24674 the header was fully editable for the Service Manager. The Lead Technician and Service Advisor fields showed active dropdown selectors (arrow_drop_down), the customer block and the asset block each showed a 'swap' (swap_horiz) control to change customer/asset, and the Mileage/Engine Hours/License Plate fields were editable input boxes (not read-only). I edited the Mileage field to 654,321, tabbed out, and after a full page reload the value persisted as 654,321 — confirming the edit saved. No permission block was encountered.
notes: STALE per spec v33: mileage etc. now gated by Work Order Lines: Create and Edit (see N1). Confirmed workOrdersCreateAndEdit AND workOrderLinesCreateAndEdit are both ON for SM, so all header/asset edits are allowed. Concrete write proof: mileage edit persisted (654,321) after reload.

what_to_do: Edit header fields; then mileage/engine hours/license plate/VIN.
expected_result: Allowed. Header = WO Create and Edit; mileage etc. = WOL Create and Edit (v33). SM has both.
spec_reference_plain: Per spec v33: work-order header fields are gated by Work Orders: Create and Edit, while asset fields (mileage, engine hours, license plate, VIN) are gated by Work Order Lines: Create and Edit. The Service Manager role holds both (workOrdersCreateAndEdit and workOrderLinesCreateAndEdit), so all of these edits should be allowed. [Ref: v33 split; checklist Service Manager row N1 'SM edits header + asset fields (WOL C&E)']
expected_plain: As a Service Manager you should be able to edit both the header fields and the asset fields (mileage, engine hours, license plate, VIN) of a work order.
actual_result_plain: On work order S9-24674 both groups of fields were editable for the Service Manager. Header: Lead Technician / Service Advisor dropdowns and customer/asset 'swap' controls were present and active. Asset fields: the Mileage, Engine Hours and License Plate fields were editable input boxes (read-only flag false). I typed 654,321 into Mileage and tabbed out; after reloading the page the Mileage input still held 654,321, proving the asset-field edit was accepted and saved. Nothing was blocked.
notes: NEW (v33) - replaces struck row #12. Confirms the v33 permission split: SM has both WO Create&Edit (header) and WOL Create&Edit (mileage/engine hours/license plate/VIN). Mileage edit persisted after reload (654,321).

expected_result: Accessible. Service Manager Customer Portal = ON (per 6/19 change).
spec_reference_plain: Per the spec (6/19 change): the Service Manager role has Customer Portal access ON (customerPortalPageAccess), so the Customer Portal entry point should be visible/accessible to the role. [Ref: SV-5319 permission matrix; checklist Service Manager row #13 'SM Customer Portal now ON']
expected_plain: As a Service Manager you should be able to reach the Customer Portal.
actual_result_plain: The Customer Portal is accessible to the Service Manager. It is exposed from the account menu (click the shop/avatar 'Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 / TS' at the top-right): the menu lists 'Customer Portal' (with a 'New' badge and an open-in-new external-link icon), alongside Billing, Settings and Logout. The entry was present and enabled (not greyed/hidden). The same menu confirmed the logged-in user is 'Tech ShopView / tech@shopview.com'.
notes: customerPortalPageAccess is ON in the Service Manager fe-permissions. The Customer Portal link lives in the account/avatar menu (top-right), not as a separate top-nav tab; it opens in a new tab (open_in_new). Direct URL /customer-portal returns the app's generic not-found page, so the intended entry point is the account-menu link.
